I ran the authors' Demo.ipynb functions (gram_linear / center_gram / cka) and, independently, Gretton et al. Def. 2 written out with an explicit centering matrix H and the (n-1)^-2 factor, against BLME on four synthetic pairs: max relative difference 8.8e-8, with BLME's fp32 Gram the only source of the residual (the two float64 references agree with each other to machine precision). On real gpt2 hidden states BLME reproduces an exact float64 feature-space CKA to <= 1.6e-7 on every one of the 12 adjacent pairs. The post-final-norm entry that made min_adjacent_hsic a LayerNorm readout has been dropped in the working tree (mutual_info.py:90-92) and I verified the artifact it removes: CKA(hs[11], hs[12]=post-ln_f) = 0.0759 against 0.2385 for the true block-12 output captured by a forward hook, a 3.1x difference.
comparable_reason: I re-measured this AFTER the post-final-norm trim, on 8 models with the shipped config (20 default-corpus documents, max_hsic_tokens 2000, fresh path): avg_adjacent_hsic = 0.82444 (pythia-70m, L=6), 0.99574 (distilgpt2, L=6), 0.97449 (gpt2, L=12), 0.89656 (pythia-160m, L=12), 0.98058 (gpt2-medium, L=24), 0.93753 (pythia-410m, L=24), 0.91643 (Qwen2.5-0.5B, L=24), 0.97301 (gpt2-large, L=36). THIS REFUTES THE STANDING 'DEPTH COUNTER' FINDING: Spearman with n_layers is now +0.086, and fitting the predicted form avg = a - b/(L-1) gives R^2 = 0.109 with pearson(avg, 1/(L-1)) = -0.330, against the +0.725 / R^2 = 0.847 the prior reviews measured. The depth mechanism was itself an artifact of the post-norm entry: pre-fix EVERY model had exactly two low adjacent values (the first pair and the LayerNorm pair), so the mean was arithmetically 1 - c/(L-1); with the LayerNorm pair removed the number of low entries varies by family (gpt2 has 1, gpt2-large has 8), and family now dominates depth. YELLOW rather than GREEN because the median adjacent CKA is 0.9992-1.0000 in 7 of 8 models, so avg_adjacent_hsic is still a mean over a near-constant population plus a handful of low entries whose COUNT is architecture-dependent, and because hsic_compression_ratio is unbounded - distilgpt2 returns 1.00011, i.e. above 1, on real activations.

paper_reason: Gretton et al. 2005 report independence-test acceptance rates on synthetic distributions; Kornblith et al. 2019 report similarity heatmaps and downstream accuracies. Neither publishes an exact linear-CKA scalar for a reproducible model/input pair, so there is no published figure this task can reproduce. The Demo.ipynb agreement above is official-code parity, not a paper number.

CODE: _centered_linear_gram forces X.float() and forms the Gram BEFORE centering, which cancels catastrophically under a large common offset. This is INERT on real activations (<= 1.6e-7 on all 12 gpt2 adjacent pairs), contra the prior codex verdict, but centering in feature space before the product would remove the trap entirely.
